title: Provably Adaptive Trust Dynamics in Context-Aware Zero-Trust Systems: A Formal Framework for Continuous Verification
tldr: Introduces ZeTHAA, a formal framework for continuous authentication and authorization that integrates contextual attributes, authentication strength, behavioral evidence, and retry dynamics into a probabilistic risk model with dual-policy thresholds to improve security-usability trade-offs.
problem_and_motivation: Existing risk-based and adaptive authentication systems often rely on heuristic scoring, lack formal continuous trust models, and fail to distinguish hard violations from probabilistic soft violations. Furthermore, they typically do not model post-login authorization, retry dynamics, or composite attack surfaces in a unified way, creating a gap between Zero-Trust principles and practical implementation.
approach: Formalizes trust as a continuous, time-evolving state variable derived from authentication strength, contextual attributes, and behavioral evidence.
Introduces a global admissibility predicate to separate non-compensable hard violations (e.g., impossible travel) from probabilistic soft violations.
Models authentication and authorization decisions using a dual-threshold policy that partitions outcomes into allow, step-up, and block regions.
Derives attribute importance dynamically from entropy and Beta-posterior distribution, enabling cold-start initialization and online recalibration.
Presents a unified composite attack surface covering credential compromise, attribute forgery, and post-grant hijacking with exponential risk escalation for retries.
Evaluates ZeTHAA on a large-scale synthetic dataset against heuristic, logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and isolation forest baselines.
Benchmarks performance against the heuristic framework of Dasu et al. and the ML-based framework of Matiushin et al.
findings: num: ZeTHAA achieved Recall and AUC exceeding 79% and 15.1% over baselines, respectively.
num: F1-Score increased by 48% to 147% compared to baseline models.
num: Efficiency improved by 20% to 65%, while reducing the cost per attack detected by up to 39.6%.
num: Against Dasu et al. and Matiushin et al., ZeTHAA showed a 57.5% lead in F1-Score and blocked 70.78% more attacks.
num: The system achieved an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 0.1981, a 33% reduction compared to the heuristic approach.
ZeTHAA produces a more expressive risk distribution, enabling effective utilization of allow, step-up, and block decision regions.
The framework blocks a significant proportion of attack events (73%) while maintaining moderate user friction.
Ablation studies confirm that attack campaign features and geographic anomalies are the most critical contextual signals.
The system exhibits robust performance under varying attack intensities (10%-40%), maintaining stable AUC and recall.
The proposed trust model demonstrates asymmetric evolution, accumulating gradually but degrading rapidly with penalties.

Table 11: Decision rates across risk regions → 73% of attacks blocked, 75% of benign events allowed, demonstrating balanced security-usability.

key_equations.explanation: Trust evolves from prior trust, context, and risk.

key_equations.equation: A(t) = \begin{cases} allow, & R(t) \leq \delta_1(R_i) \\ step\_up, & \delta_1(R_i) < R(t) \leq \delta_2(R_i) \\ deny, & R(t) > \delta_2(R_i) \end{cases}
key_equations.explanation: Dual-threshold policy maps risk to decision regions.

key_equations.equation: Pr[Attack Success | C(t)] = 1-(1 - Pr[Attack_{auth} | C(t)])(1 - Pr[Attack_{authz} | C(t)])
key_equations.explanation: Unified attack probability combining authentication and authorization phase threats.
Attribute weights derived via softmax normalization of utility scores.

definitions.definition: Zero-Trust Hybrid Adaptive Authentication, the proposed framework for continuous authentication and authorization.
Security paradigm based on 'never trust, always verify', requiring continuous evaluation of authentication and authorization.
Authenticator Assurance Level, a NIST standard metric characterizing authentication method strength (levels 1-3).
A non-compensable failure (e.g., impossible travel, cryptographic failure) that immediately terminates a session.
A probabilistic deviation from established behavioral patterns that reduces trust but does not immediately terminate the session.
Exponentially Weighted Moving Average, used for gradual profile updates in behavioral learning.
National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication defining Zero Trust Architecture principles.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a formally grounded, mathematically precise framework for continuous verification in Zero-Trust architectures, moving beyond heuristic approaches. It provides a unified model integrating authentication, authorization, and continuous monitoring with explicit handling of hard and soft violations. The work establishes a rigorous methodology for attribute weighting and penalty assignment using entropy and Bayesian learning, addressing the cold-start problem. It introduces a composite threat model that captures a broader range of attack surfaces than previous work. The comprehensive experimental evaluation against baselines and existing frameworks provides a clear benchmark for future research in adaptive authentication systems.
directly_justifies: ZeTHAA produces a more expressive risk distribution and significantly higher attack detection and efficiency while minimizing user friction.
The proposed framework demonstrates a 57.5% lead in F1-Score compared to heuristic and ML-based frameworks.
ZeTHAA provides a mathematically grounded foundation for Zero-Trust systems aligned with NIST standards.
The introduction of a global admissibility predicate enables clear separation of non-compensable hard violations from probabilistic soft violations.
Attribute importance is dynamically derived from entropy and Beta-posterior distribution, enabling robust cold-start initialization.
limits: Evaluation is conducted on a synthetic dataset, not real-world user data, which may not capture all nuances of actual user behavior.
The framework's guarantees depend on accurate attribute measurements and correct initialization of authentication strengths.
While aligned with NIST standards, the paper does not provide formal certification or real-world deployment validation.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was performed. Domains flagged as relevant included Landscape of Existing Systems (4.A), Limitations and Gaps (4.B), Behavioral Profiles (5.A), Classification Approaches (5.C), Predictive Modeling (6.A), Forecasting (6.B), Constrained Optimization (7.C), Infeasibility Handling (7.D), Cold-Start (7.E), Anomaly Detection (8.A, 8.B, 8.C), Mobile Design (9.A, 9.B), Privacy and Security (10.A, 10.B), and Evaluation Frameworks (12.A, 12.B). The paper's core focus on adaptive authentication, anomaly detection, and risk modeling directly supports these. Topics like Budgeting Strategies (7.A, 7.B) were considered but rejected as the paper does not explicitly address budget allocation; however, its policy-driven thresholds have conceptual overlap. Culturally specific financial practices (2.A, 2.B, 2.C, 2.D) were not covered as the study is general and algorithm-specific. Engagement dynamics (11.A, 11.B) and specific financial management topics (13.A, 13.B, 13.C) were not addressed. The overall topical coverage is strong in system evaluation, algorithmic modules, and foundational security modeling.

limitations: Relies on a synthetic dataset, which may not fully generalize to real-world user behavior and attack patterns.
Assumes accurate attribute observability and bounded noise, which may not hold in all real-world environments.
The learning rates and thresholds are policy-configurable and require careful tuning, which may be non-trivial.
Guarantees are contingent on correct initialization of authentication strengths and structural attribute properties.
remember_this: ZeTHAA introduces a formal, mathematically grounded framework for continuous Zero-Trust authentication and authorization.
A global admissibility predicate distinguishes hard violations from probabilistic soft violations, enabling clear enforcement.
Attribute weights and penalties are dynamically derived using entropy and Bayesian learning, addressing cold-start.
The dual-threshold policy partitions outcomes into allow, step-up, and block regions, improving security-usability trade-offs.
ZeTHAA achieved a 57.5% lead in F1-Score and blocked 70.78% more attacks than existing heuristic and ML-based frameworks.
